title: Pre-authentication stack buffer overflow in DTLS fragmented handshake reassembly (TLSe)
Zero-length BIT STRING in X.509 DER causes memcpy with size -1 (remote crash) in TLSe
Stack buffer overflow in tls_stun_parse() key construction (WebRTC/STUN, pre-auth)
TLS 1.3 client accepts Finished without CertificateVerify, enabling certificate impersonation
Chain validation ignores basicConstraints and keyUsage: a non-CA certificate can issue certificates that TLSe reports as verified
Out-of-bounds write in tls_certificate_to_string(): negative size passed to snprintf once the rendered peer certificate exceeds the caller's buffer
Client-certificate authentication is not enforced: handshake completes without a client certificate and tls_client_verified() returns true for an untrusted self-signed certificate
DTLS cookie is not bound to the client source address, allowing replay to spoofed peers and amplification
Zero-length CBC record triggers 1-byte heap out-of-bounds read (pt[-1]) in tls_parse_message
DTLS short handshake record causes out-of-bounds read of the fragment header in tls_consume_stream
Stale public-key/signature length after the key is cleared leads to a NULL pointer dereference in tls_certificate_to_string()
No DTLS anti-replay window: captured application-data records are re-delivered to the application indefinitely
